description: Towards a peer recorded Ed4, a C_PDU's last segment too long for the configured transmission length is cut to fill the length, rather than stretching the transmission for it.
note: As dts-tx-block-align-ed4 up to its data transmission, with dts.max_segment_size back at its default 1023 and dts.max_transmission_ms 5550 (one block: 600 + 4800 + 150); no end-of-message marker (modem.eom_bytes 0), so one 40-byte block carries 40 bytes. Everything before 108000 is unchanged: the 25-byte request needs one block. At 108000 the whole 50-byte C_PDU (C_PCI, DATA S_PDU header and the 44-byte U_PDU) would be one segment, its last, a 69-byte DATA-ONLY needing 2 blocks. Towards a peer recorded Ed4 any segment may be shorter than the maximum (C-0553), and the cut to the capacity applies to a last segment too (C-1155), so the transmission is not stretched for it (interp C-1042): it is cut to end at the one block's end, 40 bytes, a 21-byte segment, C_PDU START but not END. FSN 0, TX WIN UWE and TX WIN LWE, since it is the only FSN allocated (C-0176, C-0185, C-0186, C-1122), DELIVER IN ORDER as the SIS asked, EOW CAPABILITY (C-1260), EOT ceil(4950 / 500) = 10 (C-0104, C-1043). No room is left for fill (C-1154). The transmission lasts 5550 ms and ends at 113550, when dts.ack_wait/0.0.1.3 starts with dts.ack_wait_ms 60000; the other 29 bytes of the C_PDU are still queued, so csma.lbt_wait starts with lbt_wait_vdcd_ms 3000 after the own transmission (K-0074). Before corpus 0.32.0 the transmission was stretched to 2 blocks for the whole 69-byte D_PDU, 10350 ms against a 5550 ms limit.
